title: Kubernetes and OKD Cluster Architecture
summary: The control plane stores desired state in etcd and reconciles it; kubelets run pods, while Services and Routes expose them.

nodes.label: kubectl / oc
nodes.detail: Submits manifests to the API server with authenticated, authorised requests.

nodes.label: API Server
nodes.detail: Validates, authenticates and persists objects. All other components watch it rather than talking to each other.

nodes.label: etcd
nodes.detail: Consistent key-value store holding all cluster state. Run as a quorum of three or five members.

nodes.label: Scheduler
nodes.detail: Watches unscheduled pods and binds each to a node based on resources, affinity, taints and topology.

nodes.label: Controller Manager
nodes.detail: Runs controllers for Deployments, ReplicaSets and nodes. Each compares desired and actual state and acts to close the gap.

nodes.label: kubelet
nodes.detail: Watches pods assigned to its node, starts containers through the container runtime and reports status and probe results.

nodes.label: kube-proxy
nodes.detail: Programs iptables or IPVS rules so Service virtual IPs load balance to healthy pod endpoints.

nodes.label: Pods
nodes.detail: Smallest deployable unit. Containers share a network namespace and receive a cluster IP.

nodes.label: Service
nodes.detail: Gives pods a stable name and IP and selects endpoints by label.

nodes.label: Route / Ingress
nodes.detail: On OKD, a Route is served by the HAProxy-based router. Ingress is the Kubernetes equivalent, mapping hostnames to Services.

steps.title: Manifest reaches the API
steps.text: A Deployment is submitted, authenticated, validated and written to etcd as desired state.

steps.title: Controllers create pods
steps.text: The controller manager sees the Deployment and creates ReplicaSet and Pod objects.

steps.title: Scheduler binds the pod
steps.text: The scheduler picks a node that fits resource and affinity rules and records the binding.

steps.title: kubelet starts containers
steps.text: The kubelet on that node sees the pod, pulls images and starts containers via the runtime.

steps.title: Service routes traffic
steps.text: kube-proxy rules map the Service IP to ready pod endpoints.

steps.title: Route exposes externally
steps.text: A Route or Ingress maps a hostname to the Service so outside clients can reach the pods.
